rules.statement: When a test or validation check exempts allowed patterns before it searches for a forbidden one, tie each exemption to the file or command where it is legitimate rather than stripping it from every file, and add a self-test that shows the check failing on a misplaced exemption.
rules.why: An exemption applied to every file lets a future file use the allowed string where it isn't legitimate, which is the regression the check exists to catch.
rules.check: Look for allow-lists or strip/replace steps in test scripts that run over all files before a forbidden-pattern search, with no per-file or per-command key, and for a missing negative fixture proving the check can fail.

rules.statement: Don't ask a workflow command that works only in its own worktree, and never switches or edits the main checkout, to refuse to start because a root PLAN.md from another session exists in the main checkout.
rules.why: That command can't collide with the main checkout, and dropping the refusal is deliberate so a run no longer needs a clean main checkout; a legacy root PLAN.md is still continued in place by /continue-plan.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing root PLAN.md stop, confirm whether the command plans, executes and lands entirely in its own worktree and never switches the main checkout; if so, don't report it.
